text:
Cutter Gauthier is why people are talking about the Ducks, and not only in Anaheim. He has 20 points in his last 10 games, well past the 11.5 our numbers expected from his chances, and the old trade still follows him: this week Flyers general manager Daniel Briere publicly pushed back on an Elliotte Friedman report about the deal that sent Gauthier west. Sportsnet's Eric Engels wondered whether his contract might end up looking like a bargain.

The top line is a scoring machine with a leak. Captain Mikael Granlund (17 points in 10) and Beckett Sennecke (16 in 10) ride with Gauthier, and the trio has outscored teams 7-5 at 5-on-5. But it has had only 43% of the expected goals in those minutes (expected goals measure the quality of the chances), which says the finishing is carrying the process.

The bigger worry is in net. Ville Husso (.842) and Lukas Dostal (.838) have both had rough last five starts, and as a team Anaheim has allowed about 10 more goals than the chances against would suggest. Laurent Brossoit went back to San Diego anyway, after a 4-1 start in the NHL.

At 11-11-1 on a 49% share of expected goals, the record is roughly honest; it just gets there in an unusual way. Our playoff odds have the Ducks at 47%, a true coin flip after Thursday's loss in Colorado. What we'd watch: whether the saves arrive before the top line cools off.
headline: Gauthier is on fire. The goalies are not.
